config.title: Net & TCP

intro.title: Net & TCP
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple TCP server and client using Node.js's built-in 'net' module. You will learn how to create a server that listens for incoming connections and a client that can send messages to it. The core programming concept involves understanding TCP sockets for network communication and handling events like 'data' and 'connection'. You'll use key Node.js constructs such as 'net.createServer()', sockets, and event listeners to implement real-time data exchange between the server and client.
intro.usecase: The Net & TCP module in Node.js is essential for building real-time communication systems like chat applications, multiplayer games, and collaborative tools. Developers use it to create custom servers for IoT devices, enabling smart home gadgets to exchange data reliably. It's also foundational for building proxy servers, load balancers, and microservices that require direct socket connections. Understanding TCP helps optimize data transfer in financial trading platforms and streaming services where low latency and reliable connections are critical.

objectives: Construct a TCP server using the Node.js net module
Initialize a TCP client connection to communicate with a server
Implement event handlers for server connection, data, and close events
Configure server settings to listen on specific ports and addresses
Manipulate incoming data streams and send responses from the server
Integrate error handling for network connection failures
Control the lifecycle of TCP connections by properly closing sockets

steps.title: Import the net module
steps.instruction: At the top of your file, import the built-in net module using require().
steps.hint: Use require('net') to import the module. This gives you access to TCP networking functionality.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: importing another built-in module
const fs = require('fs');
steps.expectedOutcome: The net module is imported and ready to use for creating TCP servers and clients.
successCriteria: The net module is imported using require('net') at the top of the file.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using require('net') exactly as shown.
steps.feedbackWrong: The net module import is missing or incorrect. Use require('net') to import the TCP networking module.

steps.title: Create a TCP server using net.createServer()
steps.instruction: Create a server variable by calling net.createServer() and assign it to a constant named 'server'.
steps.hint: Use the net module you imported to call its createServer method.
steps.analogousExample:
// Creating a server instance
const server = net.createServer();
steps.expectedOutcome: A server variable is created using net.createServer()
successCriteria: The code contains a constant named 'server' assigned to net.createServer()
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're calling net.createServer() and assigning it to a constant named 'server'.
steps.feedbackWrong: That doesn't look right. You need to create a server instance using net.createServer() and assign it to a variable.

steps.title: Define the server connection event handler
steps.instruction: Add a connection event listener to the server that receives a socket parameter. The listener should be a function that takes a socket parameter.
steps.hint: Use server.on('connection', (socket) => { ... }) to handle new client connections.
steps.expectedOutcome: The server now has a connection event listener that will execute when a client connects.
successCriteria: A connection event listener is added to the server with a function that receives a socket parameter.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added an event listener, but make sure it's for the 'connection' event and receives a socket parameter.
steps.feedbackWrong: The connection event listener is missing or incorrect. Use server.on('connection', (socket) => { ... }).

steps.title: Handle incoming data from clients
steps.instruction: Inside the connection event handler, add a data event listener to the socket parameter to receive client messages. The listener should log the received data as a string.
steps.hint: Use socket.on('data', callback) where the callback receives the data parameter. Convert the data to a string using data.toString().
steps.expectedOutcome: The server will now log any data sent by connected clients.
successCriteria: A data event listener is added inside the connection handler that logs received client data as a string.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a listener, but make sure it's inside the connection handler and logs the data as a string.
steps.feedbackWrong: The data event listener is missing or incorrectly placed. Add socket.on('data', callback) inside the connection handler.

steps.title: Send data back to the client
steps.instruction: Inside the data event handler, use socket.write() to echo the received data back to the client.
steps.hint: Call socket.write() with the data parameter inside the data event handler.
steps.expectedOutcome: The server will now echo any data it receives back to the connected client.
successCriteria: The data event handler includes a socket.write() call that sends the received data back to the client.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're calling socket.write() inside the data event handler with the received data parameter.
steps.feedbackWrong: Try again. You need to add a socket.write() call inside the data event handler to send the received data back to the client.

steps.title: Start the server listening on a port
steps.instruction: Call the server.listen() method with port 3000 and a callback function that logs 'Server listening on port 3000' when the server starts.
steps.hint: The listen method takes a port number and an optional callback that runs when the server is ready.
steps.expectedOutcome: The server will be configured to listen for incoming connections on port 3000, and a confirmation message will be logged when it starts.
successCriteria: server.listen() is called with port 3000 and a callback function that logs the listening message.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're calling server.listen() with both the port number (3000) and a callback function that logs the message.
steps.feedbackWrong: The server isn't configured to listen yet. You need to call server.listen() with port 3000 and a callback.

steps.title: Create a TCP client using net.createConnection()
steps.instruction: Create a client variable by calling net.createConnection() with port 3000 and host 'localhost' as parameters.
steps.hint: Use net.createConnection() and pass an object with port and host properties.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: creating a connection to a server
const client = net.createConnection({ port: 8080, host: 'localhost' });
steps.expectedOutcome: A client variable is created using net.createConnection() with the specified port and host.
successCriteria: The client variable is created using net.createConnection() with port 3000 and host 'localhost'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using net.createConnection() with the correct port and host parameters.
steps.feedbackWrong: The client wasn't created correctly. Check that you're using net.createConnection() with port 3000 and host 'localhost'.

steps.title: Handle client connection events
steps.instruction: Add a 'connect' event listener to the client to log a success message when the connection is established.
steps.hint: Use the client.on('connect', callback) method. Inside the callback, log a message like 'Client connected to server'.
steps.expectedOutcome: The client will log a success message when it successfully connects to the server.
successCriteria: The client has a 'connect' event listener that logs a success message.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're adding the event listener to the client object and logging a message inside the callback.
steps.feedbackWrong: The client needs a 'connect' event listener. Use client.on('connect', callback) to handle successful connections.

steps.title: Send data from client to server
steps.instruction: Inside the client's connect event handler, use client.write() to send a test message to the server.
steps.hint: After the client connects, you can send data by calling write() on the client object with a string message.
steps.expectedOutcome: The client will send a test message to the server immediately after establishing a connection.
successCriteria: The client's connect event handler includes a call to client.write() with a test message string.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're calling client.write() inside the connect event handler with a string message.
steps.feedbackWrong: The client isn't sending data to the server. Add client.write('your message') inside the connect event handler.

steps.title: Handle data received from the server
steps.instruction: Add a data event listener to the client to handle data received from the server. Inside the listener, log the received data to the console.
steps.hint: Use the client.on('data', ...) method to listen for incoming data from the server. The callback function receives the data as a parameter.
steps.expectedOutcome: The client will now listen for data sent from the server and log it to the console when received.
successCriteria: A data event listener is added to the client that logs received data to the console.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've added the data event listener to the client and included console.log to display the received data.
steps.feedbackWrong: The client doesn't have a data event listener yet. Add client.on('data', ...) to handle incoming data from the server.
